records.literal_gloss: And said [the] king of Israel to Jehoshaphat, disguising myself and going into the battle, and you, wear your garments. And disguised himself [the] king of Israel, and they went into the battle.

en.L: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "[I will] disguise myself and go into the battle, but you, put on your robes." And the king of Israel disguised himself, and they went into the battle.
en.B: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will go into the battle in disguise, but you should put on your royal robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself, and the two of them went into the fight.
en.R: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will dress like an ordinary soldier when I go into battle, but you should wear your royal robes." So the king of Israel put on a disguise, and the two kings went to fight.

es.L: Y el rey de Israel dijo a Josafat: «Yo me disfrazaré y entraré en la batalla, pero tú ponte tus vestiduras». Y el rey de Israel se disfrazó, y entraron en la batalla.
es.B: El rey de Israel le dijo a Josafat: «Yo entraré en la batalla disfrazado, pero tú ponte tus vestiduras reales». Así que el rey de Israel se disfrazó, y los dos entraron en la batalla.
es.R: El rey de Israel le dijo a Josafat: «Yo me vestiré como un soldado cualquiera para entrar en la batalla, pero tú ponte tus ropas reales». Así que el rey de Israel se disfrazó, y los dos reyes fueron a pelear.

fr.L: Et le roi d’Israël dit à Josaphat : « [Je vais] me déguiser et entrer dans la bataille, mais toi, revêts tes habits. » Et le roi d’Israël se déguisa, et ils entrèrent dans la bataille.
fr.B: Le roi d’Israël dit à Josaphat : « Je vais me déguiser pour aller au combat, mais toi, revêts tes habits royaux. » Le roi d’Israël se déguisa donc, et ils allèrent tous deux au combat.
fr.R: Le roi d’Israël a dit à Josaphat : « Je vais m’habiller comme un simple soldat pour aller à la bataille, mais toi, mets tes habits royaux. » Le roi d’Israël s’est donc déguisé, et les deux rois sont allés se battre.

sw.L: Mfalme wa Israeli akamwambia Yehoshafati, "Nitajibadilisha na kuingia vitani, lakini wewe, vaa mavazi yako." Mfalme wa Israeli akajibadilisha, nao wakaingia vitani.
sw.B: Mfalme wa Israeli akamwambia Yehoshafati, "Nitaingia vitani nikiwa nimejibadilisha, lakini wewe vaa mavazi yako ya kifalme." Basi mfalme wa Israeli akajibadilisha, nao wawili wakaingia vitani.
sw.R: Mfalme wa Israeli akamwambia Yehoshafati, "Nitavaa kama askari wa kawaida nitakapoingia vitani, lakini wewe vaa mavazi yako ya kifalme." Basi mfalme wa Israeli akajificha kwa mavazi, na wafalme hao wawili wakaenda kupigana.

vi.L: Vua Y-sơ-ra-ên nói với Giô-sa-phát: "[Tôi sẽ] cải trang và đi vào trận, còn vua, hãy mặc triều phục của vua." Vua Y-sơ-ra-ên cải trang, và họ đi vào trận.
vi.B: Vua Y-sơ-ra-ên nói với Giô-sa-phát: "Tôi sẽ cải trang mà ra trận, còn vua thì cứ mặc triều phục." Vậy vua Y-sơ-ra-ên cải trang, và cả hai vua ra trận.
vi.R: Vua Y-sơ-ra-ên nói với Giô-sa-phát: "Tôi sẽ ăn mặc như một người lính thường khi ra trận, còn vua thì cứ mặc triều phục." Vậy vua Y-sơ-ra-ên cải trang, và hai vua ra trận.

ko.L: 그리고 이스라엘 왕이 여호사밧에게 말했다. "나는 변장하고 싸움터에 들어가겠소. 그러나 당신은 당신의 예복을 입으시오." 그리고 이스라엘 왕은 변장했고, 그들이 싸움터에 들어갔다.
ko.B: 이스라엘 왕이 여호사밧에게 말했다. "나는 변장하고 싸움터에 들어가겠소. 그러나 당신은 왕의 예복을 입으시오." 이스라엘 왕은 변장했고, 두 사람은 싸움터에 들어갔다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 왕이 여호사밧에게 말했다. "나는 보통 군인처럼 옷을 입고 싸움터에 들어가겠소. 그러나 당신은 왕의 예복을 입으시오." 그래서 이스라엘 왕은 변장을 했고, 두 왕은 싸우러 들어갔다.

pt.L: E o rei de Israel disse a Josafá: "[Vou] me disfarçar e entrar na batalha, mas você, vista os seus mantos." E o rei de Israel se disfarçou, e entraram na batalha.
pt.B: O rei de Israel disse a Josafá: "Vou entrar na batalha disfarçado, mas você deve vestir os seus mantos reais." Assim o rei de Israel se disfarçou, e os dois entraram na luta.
pt.R: O rei de Israel disse a Josafá: "Vou me vestir como um soldado comum quando entrar na batalha, mas você deve usar os seus mantos reais." Então o rei de Israel se disfarçou, e os dois reis foram lutar.

decisions.choice: "they went" where 1 Kings 22:30 has "he went"
decisions.reason: In Kings the king of Israel disguises himself and goes into the battle. Chronicles has the plural, "and they went into the battle": both kings went. Otherwise the verse is the same as 1 Kings 22:30.

decisions.choice: disguising myself and going: an infinitive used as a statement of intention
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses two infinitives, a short, clipped way of saying "I will disguise myself and go".

decisions.choice: the king's disguise: an attempt to escape the prophecy
decisions.reason: Ahab tries to make himself unrecognizable so that he cannot be singled out, perhaps having heard of the Aramean order (verse 30) or fearing Micaiah's word. Jehoshaphat, in royal robes, becomes the obvious target (verse 31). Saul too disguised himself before his final battle (1 Samuel 28:8), and Josiah would later do the same (35:22).

decisions.choice: dress like an ordinary soldier
decisions.reason: Readable says what the disguise was for, the first time; it then uses "disguised".

decisions.choice: the two of them / the two kings
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that "they" are both kings (m1).

decisions.choice: e entraram (L), e os dois entraram (B), e os dois reis foram lutar (R)
decisions.reason: As 1 Kings 22:30 in Portuguese, with the plural verb of Chronicles: both kings went into the battle (m1).

source.text: וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֡ם צִוָּה֩ אֶת־שָׂרֵ֨י הָרֶ֤כֶב אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֚א תִּלָּ֣חֲמ֔וּ אֶת־הַקָּטֹ֖ן אֶת־הַגָּד֑וֹל כִּ֛י אִֽם־אֶת־מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְבַדּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] king of Aram had commanded [the] commanders of the chariotry that [were] his, saying, not you shall fight with the small, with the great, but with [the] king of Israel by himself.

en.L: And the king of Aram had commanded the commanders of the chariots that [were] his, saying, "Do not fight with the small [or] the great, but only with the king of Israel alone."
en.B: Now the king of Aram had given an order to his chariot commanders: "Fight with no one, small or great, but the king of Israel alone."
en.R: The king of Aram had given orders to his chariot commanders: "Do not attack anyone except the king of Israel."

es.L: Y el rey de Aram había mandado a los jefes de sus carros, diciendo: «No {{plural_you:peleen|peleéis}} ni con chico ni con grande, sino solo con el rey de Israel».
es.B: El rey de Aram había dado esta orden a los jefes de sus carros: «No {{plural_you:peleen|peleéis}} con nadie, ni chico ni grande, sino solo con el rey de Israel».
es.R: El rey de Aram había dado órdenes a los jefes de sus carros: «No {{plural_you:ataquen|ataquéis}} a nadie más que al rey de Israel».

fr.L: Et le roi d’Aram avait ordonné aux chefs des chars qui [étaient] à lui, en disant : « Ne combattez ni petit [ni] grand, mais seulement le roi d’Israël. »
fr.B: Or le roi d’Aram avait donné cet ordre à ses chefs de chars : « N’attaquez personne, petit ou grand, sauf le roi d’Israël. »
fr.R: Le roi d’Aram avait donné cet ordre à ses chefs de chars : « N’attaquez personne d’autre que le roi d’Israël. »

sw.L: Mfalme wa Aramu alikuwa amewaamuru wakuu wa magari yake ya vita, akisema, "Msipigane na mdogo [wala] na mkubwa, ila na mfalme wa Israeli peke yake."
sw.B: Mfalme wa Aramu alikuwa amewapa wakuu wake wa magari ya vita amri hii: "Msipigane na mtu yeyote, mdogo au mkubwa, ila mfalme wa Israeli peke yake."
sw.R: Mfalme wa Aramu alikuwa amewapa wakuu wake wa magari ya vita amri hii: "Msimshambulie mtu yeyote isipokuwa mfalme wa Israeli."

vi.L: Vua A-ram đã truyền lệnh cho các tướng chỉ huy xe chiến mã của mình rằng: "Đừng giao chiến với ai, nhỏ [hay] lớn, ngoại trừ một mình vua Y-sơ-ra-ên."
vi.B: Bấy giờ vua A-ram đã ra lệnh cho các tướng chỉ huy xe chiến mã của mình: "Đừng đánh ai cả, dù nhỏ hay lớn, chỉ đánh một mình vua Y-sơ-ra-ên thôi."
vi.R: Vua A-ram đã ra lệnh cho các tướng chỉ huy xe chiến mã của mình: "Đừng tấn công ai cả, chỉ tấn công vua Y-sơ-ra-ên mà thôi."

ko.L: 그리고 아람 왕이 자기에게 속한 병거 지휘관들에게 명령하여 말했다. "작은 자나 큰 자나 [누구와도] 싸우지 말고, 오직 이스라엘 왕하고만 싸워라."
ko.B: 그런데 아람 왕은 자기 병거 지휘관들에게 이렇게 명령해 두었다. "작은 자든 큰 자든 아무하고도 싸우지 말고, 오직 이스라엘 왕만 공격하여라."
ko.R: 아람 왕은 자기 병거 지휘관들에게 명령해 두었다. "이스라엘 왕 말고는 아무도 공격하지 말아라."

pt.L: E o rei de Arã tinha ordenado aos comandantes dos carros que [eram] seus, dizendo: "Não lutem com o pequeno [nem com] o grande, mas somente com o rei de Israel."
pt.B: O rei de Arã tinha dado uma ordem aos seus comandantes de carros: "Não lutem com ninguém, pequeno ou grande, a não ser com o rei de Israel."
pt.R: O rei de Arã tinha dado ordens aos seus comandantes de carros de guerra: "Não ataquem ninguém, a não ser o rei de Israel."

decisions.choice: no number of commanders, where 1 Kings 22:31 has "thirty-two"
decisions.reason: Chronicles does not give the number of the chariot commanders, which Kings links to the thirty-two kings of 1 Kings 20:1, 24. It also says "with the small, with the great" without "or". The order is the same as in 1 Kings 22:31.

decisions.choice: small and great: anyone at all
decisions.reason: Naming the two extremes means everyone. The Aramean chariots are to ignore every other soldier and hunt down the king.

decisions.choice: the king of Israel alone: the target is the king
decisions.reason: Killing the enemy king would end the battle. The order explains Ahab's disguise and the danger to Jehoshaphat in his royal robes.

decisions.choice: [or]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "or", which English needs between the two words. Readable drops the pair "small or great" and says "anyone" (m2).

decisions.choice: without "trinta e dois"; com o pequeno [nem com] o grande (L)
decisions.reason: As 1 Kings 22:31 in Portuguese, without the number of commanders, which Chronicles does not give, and at Literal with the two words joined without "or" (m1).

source.text: וַיְהִ֡י כִּרְאוֹת֩ שָׂרֵ֨י הָרֶ֜כֶב אֶת־יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט וְהֵ֤מָּה אָֽמְרוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל ה֔וּא וַיָּסֹ֥בּוּ עָלָ֖יו לְהִלָּחֵ֑ם וַיִּזְעַ֤ק יְהֽוֹשָׁפָט֙ וַֽיהוָ֣ה עֲזָר֔וֹ וַיְסִיתֵ֥ם אֱלֹהִ֖ים מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when saw [the] commanders of the chariotry Jehoshaphat, and they said, [the] king of Israel [is] he; and they surrounded him to fight, and cried out Jehoshaphat, and Yahweh helped him, and enticed them God away from him.

en.L: And it happened, when the commanders of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, that they said, "He [is] the king of Israel." And they surrounded him to fight, and Jehoshaphat cried out, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} helped him, and God drew them away from him.
en.B: When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, "That is the king of Israel!" So they closed in on him to attack, and Jehoshaphat cried out. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} helped him; God drew them away from him.
en.R: When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat in his royal robes, they said, "That is the king of Israel!" So they surrounded him to attack him. But Jehoshaphat cried out, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} helped him. God made them turn away from him.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando los jefes de los carros vieron a Josafat, dijeron: «Este [es] el rey de Israel». Y lo rodearon para pelear, y Josafat gritó, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo ayudó, y Dios los apartó de él.
es.B: Cuando los jefes de los carros vieron a Josafat, dijeron: «¡Ese es el rey de Israel!». Así que lo rodearon para atacarlo, y Josafat gritó. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo ayudó; Dios los apartó de él.
es.R: Cuando los jefes de los carros vieron a Josafat con sus ropas reales, dijeron: «¡Ese es el rey de Israel!». Así que lo rodearon para atacarlo. Pero Josafat gritó pidiendo ayuda, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo ayudó. Dios hizo que se apartaran de él.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand les chefs des chars virent Josaphat, qu’ils dirent : « C’[est] le roi d’Israël. » Et ils l’entourèrent pour l’attaquer, et Josaphat poussa un cri, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} le secourut, et Dieu les détourna de lui.
fr.B: Quand les chefs des chars virent Josaphat, ils dirent : « C’est le roi d’Israël ! » Ils l’entourèrent donc pour l’attaquer, et Josaphat poussa un cri. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} le secourut ; Dieu les détourna de lui.
fr.R: Quand les chefs des chars ont vu Josaphat dans ses habits royaux, ils ont dit : « C’est le roi d’Israël ! » Alors ils l’ont entouré pour l’attaquer. Mais Josaphat a crié, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a secouru. Dieu les a fait s’éloigner de lui.

sw.L: Ikawa, wakuu wa magari ya vita walipomwona Yehoshafati, wakasema, "Yeye [ndiye] mfalme wa Israeli." Wakamzunguka ili kupigana, na Yehoshafati akapiga kelele, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamsaidia, na Mungu akawavuta mbali naye.
sw.B: Wakuu wa magari ya vita walipomwona Yehoshafati, walisema, "Huyo ndiye mfalme wa Israeli!" Basi wakamzunguka ili kumshambulia, naye Yehoshafati akapiga kelele. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamsaidia; Mungu akawavuta mbali naye.
sw.R: Wakuu wa magari ya vita walipomwona Yehoshafati katika mavazi yake ya kifalme, walisema, "Huyo ndiye mfalme wa Israeli!" Basi wakamzunguka ili kumshambulia. Lakini Yehoshafati akapiga kelele, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamsaidia. Mungu akawafanya wageuke waondoke kwake.

vi.L: Xảy ra, khi các tướng chỉ huy xe chiến mã thấy Giô-sa-phát, họ nói: "Đó [là] vua Y-sơ-ra-ên." Họ vây quanh ông để tấn công, và Giô-sa-phát kêu lên; {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giúp đỡ ông, và Đức Chúa Trời dụ họ rời xa ông.
vi.B: Khi các tướng chỉ huy xe chiến mã thấy Giô-sa-phát, họ nói: "Đó là vua Y-sơ-ra-ên!" Vậy họ vây quanh ông để tấn công, và Giô-sa-phát kêu lên. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giúp đỡ ông; Đức Chúa Trời khiến họ rời xa ông.
vi.R: Khi các tướng chỉ huy xe chiến mã thấy Giô-sa-phát mặc triều phục, họ nói: "Đó là vua Y-sơ-ra-ên!" Vậy họ vây quanh để tấn công ông. Nhưng Giô-sa-phát kêu lên, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giúp đỡ ông. Đức Chúa Trời khiến họ quay đi khỏi ông.

ko.L: 그리고 병거 지휘관들이 여호사밧을 보았을 때, 그들이 "그가 이스라엘 왕이다" 하고 말하며 그와 싸우려고 그를 에워쌌다. 그러자 여호사밧이 부르짖었고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그를 도우셨으며, 하나님께서 그들을 그에게서 떠나게 하셨다.
ko.B: 병거 지휘관들은 여호사밧을 보고 "저 사람이 이스라엘 왕이다!" 하고 말하며 그를 공격하려고 에워쌌다. 그러자 여호사밧이 부르짖었고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그를 도우셨다. 하나님께서 그들을 그에게서 떠나가게 하셨다.
ko.R: 병거 지휘관들은 왕의 예복을 입은 여호사밧을 보고 말했다. "저 사람이 이스라엘 왕이다!" 그래서 그들은 그를 공격하려고 에워쌌다. 그러나 여호사밧이 부르짖자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그를 도우셨다. 하나님께서 그들이 그에게서 돌아서게 하셨다.

pt.L: E aconteceu que, quando os comandantes dos carros viram Josafá, disseram: "Ele [é] o rei de Israel." E o cercaram para lutar, e Josafá gritou, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} o ajudou, e Deus os atraiu para longe dele.
pt.B: Quando os comandantes dos carros viram Josafá, disseram: "Aquele é o rei de Israel!" Então o cercaram para atacá-lo, e Josafá gritou. {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} o ajudou; Deus os afastou dele.
pt.R: Quando os comandantes dos carros de guerra viram Josafá com os seus mantos reais, disseram: "Aquele é o rei de Israel!" Então o cercaram para atacá-lo. Mas Josafá gritou, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} o ajudou. Deus fez com que eles se afastassem dele.

decisions.choice: "and Yahweh helped him; God drew them away from him", added to 1 Kings 22:32
decisions.reason: Kings tells only that Jehoshaphat cried out; the next verse tells that the commanders turned back when they saw he was not the king of Israel. Chronicles adds that Yahweh helped him and that God drew the attackers away, so Jehoshaphat's cry is a cry to Yahweh and his escape is Yahweh's answer. Chronicles also lacks "surely" ("surely he is the king of Israel") and says the commanders "surrounded" him where Kings says they "turned aside" against him.

decisions.choice: cried out ... Yahweh helped him: the God who answers those who call on him
decisions.reason: Chronicles often tells how those who cried to Yahweh in battle were heard and helped (1 Chronicles 5:20; 2 Chronicles 13:14-15; 14:10). Jehoshaphat had joined Ahab's war, but in his danger he called on Yahweh and was saved.

decisions.choice: drew them away: the same verb as "enticed" in verse 2
decisions.reason: The verb means to urge or lure. In verse 2 Ahab lured Jehoshaphat into the war; here God lures the enemy chariots away from him.

decisions.choice: surrounded: closed in on him
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn or go around; with "against" it describes the chariots wheeling round to close in on Jehoshaphat.

decisions.choice: in his royal robes
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader why they took him for the king (verse 29), as in 1 Kings 22:32.

decisions.choice: made them turn away
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what God's luring them away meant (m3): the commanders turned away from Jehoshaphat.

decisions.choice: "los apartó" (L, B); "hizo que se apartaran" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one of verse 2, "enticed" (meaning decision); Spanish cannot keep one verb for both senses here and says what God did.

decisions.choice: "dụ họ rời xa" (L); "khiến họ rời xa" (B), "khiến họ quay đi" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one translated "dụ" in verse 2 (m3); Literal keeps it to show the echo, Balanced and Readable say what happened.

decisions.choice: "부르짖었고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그를 도우셨으며, 하나님께서 ... 떠나게 하셨다"
decisions.reason: Chronicles adds that the LORD helped him and God drew them away; Korean takes "부르짖다", the verb for crying to God, and adds the clause.

decisions.choice: as 1 Kings 22:32, with "o cercaram" and the added "o SENHOR o ajudou, e Deus os atraiu (L) / afastou (B) para longe dele"
decisions.reason: The first half keeps the Portuguese of 1 Kings 22:32, without its "certamente", which Chronicles lacks, and with "cercaram" for Chronicles' "surrounded" (m4). The words Chronicles adds (m1) are new: Literal says "os atraiu", the verb of verse 2 (m3), Balanced and Readable say plainly that God turned them away.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י כִּרְאוֹת֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב כִּ֥י לֹא־הָיָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ מֵאַחֲרָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when saw [the] commanders of the chariotry that not was [it the] king of Israel, and they turned back from after him.

en.L: And it happened, when the commanders of the chariots saw that it was not the king of Israel, that they turned back from pursuing him.
en.B: Once the chariot commanders saw he was not Israel's king, they broke off the chase.
en.R: When the chariot commanders realized he was not the king of Israel, they stopped chasing him.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando los jefes de los carros vieron que no [era] el rey de Israel, dejaron de perseguirlo.
es.B: En cuanto los jefes de los carros vieron que no era el rey de Israel, dejaron de perseguirlo.
es.R: Cuando los jefes de los carros se dieron cuenta de que no era el rey de Israel, dejaron de perseguirlo.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand les chefs des chars virent que ce n’[était] pas le roi d’Israël, qu’ils se détournèrent de lui.
fr.B: Dès que les chefs des chars virent que ce n’était pas le roi d’Israël, ils cessèrent de le poursuivre.
fr.R: Quand les chefs des chars ont compris que ce n’était pas le roi d’Israël, ils ont arrêté de le poursuivre.

sw.L: Ikawa, wakuu wa magari ya vita walipoona kwamba yeye si mfalme wa Israeli, wakarudi wasimfuatie.
sw.B: Wakuu wa magari ya vita walipoona kwamba yeye si mfalme wa Israeli, waliacha kumfukuza.
sw.R: Wakuu wa magari ya vita walipotambua kwamba yeye si mfalme wa Israeli, waliacha kumfukuza.

vi.L: Xảy ra, khi các tướng chỉ huy xe chiến mã thấy ông không phải là vua Y-sơ-ra-ên, họ quay trở lại, không đuổi theo ông nữa.
vi.B: Khi các tướng chỉ huy xe chiến mã thấy ông không phải là vua Y-sơ-ra-ên, họ thôi không đuổi theo nữa.
vi.R: Khi các tướng chỉ huy xe chiến mã nhận ra ông không phải là vua Y-sơ-ra-ên, họ không đuổi theo ông nữa.

ko.L: 그리고 병거 지휘관들이 그가 이스라엘 왕이 아닌 것을 보았을 때, 그들이 그를 뒤쫓다가 돌아섰다.
ko.B: 병거 지휘관들은 그가 이스라엘 왕이 아닌 것을 알고 그를 뒤쫓다가 돌아섰다.
ko.R: 병거 지휘관들은 그가 이스라엘 왕이 아니라는 것을 알고 더 이상 쫓지 않았다.

pt.L: E aconteceu que, quando os comandantes dos carros viram que não era o rei de Israel, deixaram de persegui-lo.
pt.B: Quando os comandantes dos carros viram que ele não era o rei de Israel, desistiram de persegui-lo.
pt.R: Quando os comandantes dos carros de guerra perceberam que ele não era o rei de Israel, pararam de persegui-lo.

decisions.choice: the same words as 1 Kings 22:33
decisions.reason: Chronicles says "that it was not the king of Israel" where Kings says "that he was not the king of Israel"; the sense is the same. In Chronicles this follows God's drawing them away (verse 31).

decisions.choice: turned back from after him: stopped pursuing him
decisions.reason: "From after him" means from following him; the commanders broke off the chase, as their orders required (verse 30).

decisions.choice: realized
decisions.reason: Readable says "realized" for "saw", since they understood rather than looked.

decisions.choice: que não era o rei de Israel (L)
decisions.reason: As 1 Kings 22:33 in Portuguese; Chronicles says "that it was not" (m1), which Portuguese says without a subject and without brackets.

source.text: וְאִ֗ישׁ מָשַׁ֤ךְ בַּקֶּ֨שֶׁת֙ לְתֻמּ֔וֹ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת־מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בֵּ֥ין הַדְּבָקִ֖ים וּבֵ֣ין הַשִּׁרְיָ֑ן וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָֽרַכָּ֗ב הֲפֹ֧ךְ יָדְךָ֛ וְהוֹצֵאתַ֥נִי מִן־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה כִּ֥י הָחֳלֵֽיתִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And a man drew on the bow in his innocence and struck [the] king of Israel between the scales and between the armor; and he said to the chariot driver, turn your hand and bring me out from the camp, for I am wounded.

en.L: And a man drew the bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the joints of the armor and the breastplate. And he said to the chariot driver, "Turn your hand and take me out of the camp, for I am wounded."
en.B: But a man drew his bow at random and hit the king of Israel between the joints of his scale armor and the breastplate. The king said to the chariot driver, "Turn around and get me out of the battle, because I am wounded."
en.R: But an Aramean soldier shot an arrow without aiming at anyone in particular. It hit the king of Israel where his armor joined together. The king said to the driver of his chariot, "Turn around and take me away from the fighting! I am wounded."

es.L: Y un hombre tensó el arco al azar e hirió al rey de Israel entre las junturas de la armadura y la coraza. Y él dijo al conductor del carro: «Vuelve tu mano y sácame del campamento, porque estoy herido».
es.B: Pero un hombre disparó su arco al azar e hirió al rey de Israel entre las junturas de su armadura de escamas y la coraza. El rey le dijo al conductor del carro: «Da la vuelta y sácame de la batalla, porque estoy herido».
es.R: Pero un soldado arameo disparó una flecha sin apuntar a nadie en particular. La flecha hirió al rey de Israel donde se unían las piezas de su armadura. El rey le dijo al conductor de su carro: «¡Da la vuelta y sácame de la pelea! Estoy herido».

fr.L: Et un homme tira de l’arc au hasard et frappa le roi d’Israël entre les jointures de l’armure et la cuirasse. Et il dit au conducteur de char : « Tourne ta main et fais-moi sortir du camp, car je suis blessé. »
fr.B: Mais un homme tira une flèche au hasard et atteignit le roi d’Israël entre les jointures de sa cotte d’écailles et sa cuirasse. Le roi dit au conducteur du char : « Fais demi-tour et sors-moi de la bataille, car je suis blessé. »
fr.R: Mais un soldat araméen a tiré une flèche sans viser personne en particulier. La flèche a atteint le roi d’Israël à l’endroit où les pièces de son armure se rejoignaient. Le roi a dit au conducteur de son char : « Fais demi-tour et emmène-moi loin des combats ! Je suis blessé. »

sw.L: Mtu mmoja akavuta upinde wake bila kukusudia, akampiga mfalme wa Israeli kati ya viungo vya deraya na kifuko cha kifua. Akamwambia dereva wa gari lake, "Geuza mkono wako, unitoe kambini, kwa maana nimejeruhiwa."
sw.B: Lakini mtu mmoja akavuta upinde wake bila kulenga mtu fulani, akampiga mfalme wa Israeli kati ya viungo vya deraya yake ya magamba na kifuko cha kifua. Mfalme akamwambia dereva wa gari lake, "Geuza unitoe vitani, kwa sababu nimejeruhiwa."
sw.R: Lakini askari mmoja wa Kiaramu akapiga mshale bila kumlenga mtu yeyote hasa. Mshale ukampiga mfalme wa Israeli mahali ambapo vipande vya deraya yake viliungana. Mfalme akamwambia dereva wa gari lake, "Geuza uniondoe vitani! Nimejeruhiwa."

vi.L: Có một người tình cờ giương cung bắn trúng vua Y-sơ-ra-ên giữa chỗ nối của áo giáp và tấm che ngực. Vua nói với người đánh xe: "Hãy quay tay lại và đưa ta ra khỏi trại quân, vì ta bị thương rồi."
vi.B: Nhưng có một người tình cờ giương cung bắn, trúng vua Y-sơ-ra-ên ngay chỗ nối giữa các mảnh giáp và tấm che ngực. Vua bảo người đánh xe: "Hãy quay xe lại và đưa ta ra khỏi trận, vì ta bị thương rồi."
vi.R: Nhưng có một người lính A-ram bắn tên mà không nhắm vào ai cả. Mũi tên trúng vua Y-sơ-ra-ên ngay chỗ các mảnh áo giáp nối với nhau. Vua bảo người đánh xe: "Hãy quay xe lại và đưa ta ra khỏi trận! Ta bị thương rồi."

ko.L: 그리고 한 사람이 무심코 활을 당겨 이스라엘 왕의 갑옷 이음새와 가슴받이 사이를 맞혔다. 그러자 그가 병거 모는 자에게 말했다. "네 손을 돌려 나를 진에서 데리고 나가거라. 내가 부상을 입었다."
ko.B: 그런데 한 군사가 무심코 활을 당겼는데, 그 화살이 이스라엘 왕의 비늘 갑옷 이음새와 가슴받이 사이를 맞혔다. 왕이 병거 모는 병사에게 말했다. "병거를 돌려 나를 싸움터에서 빠져나가게 하여라. 내가 부상을 입었다."
ko.R: 그런데 아람 군인 하나가 아무나 겨누지 않고 활을 쏘았다. 그 화살이 이스라엘 왕의 갑옷 이음새를 맞혔다. 왕이 자기 병거를 모는 병사에게 말했다. "병거를 돌려 나를 싸움터에서 데리고 나가거라! 내가 다쳤다."

pt.L: E um homem puxou o arco ao acaso e atingiu o rei de Israel entre as juntas da armadura e a couraça. E ele disse ao condutor do carro: "Vire a sua mão e tire-me do acampamento, porque estou ferido."
pt.B: Mas um homem puxou o arco ao acaso e atingiu o rei de Israel entre as juntas da sua armadura de escamas e a couraça. O rei disse ao condutor do carro: "Dê a volta e tire-me da batalha, porque estou ferido."
pt.R: Mas um soldado arameu atirou uma flecha sem mirar em ninguém. A flecha atingiu o rei de Israel bem onde as partes da armadura se juntavam. O rei disse ao condutor do seu carro: "Dê a volta e tire-me da luta! Estou ferido."

decisions.choice: the same account as 1 Kings 22:34
decisions.reason: The verse matches 1 Kings 22:34. Chronicles says "the chariot driver" where Kings says "his chariot driver", and has "your hand" in a slightly different form; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: in his innocence: at random, without aiming at the king
decisions.reason: The word means simplicity or innocence. The archer shot without a particular target and with no idea who he hit. What the Aramean commanders failed to do with their orders, one unaimed arrow did, as Micaiah had said.

decisions.choice: between the scales and the armor: at a gap where pieces of armor met
alternatives: between the joints and the coat of mail
between the lower armor and the breastplate
decisions.reason: The two words are rare and their exact meaning is not certain. The first, from a root meaning "to cling, to join", may name the joints or the small overlapping plates of scale armor; the second names a coat of mail or breastplate. The arrow struck at a weak point where they met, perhaps under the arm or at the waist.

decisions.choice: turn your hand: turn the chariot around
decisions.reason: The driver holds the reins in his hand; to turn his hand is to turn the horses.

decisions.choice: the camp: the army, the battle lines
decisions.reason: Here "camp" means the army drawn up in battle, so to be taken out of it is to leave the fighting.

decisions.choice: an Aramean soldier
decisions.reason: Readable says that the archer was one of the enemy, which the context makes plain.

decisions.choice: joints ... breastplate / where his armor joined together
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced name the two parts of the armor; Readable gives the sense that matters, a gap in the armor (m3).

decisions.choice: ao condutor do carro (L, B)
decisions.reason: As 1 Kings 22:34 in Portuguese, with "the chariot driver" for Kings' "his chariot driver" (m1).

source.text: וַתַּ֤עַל הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וּמֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הָיָ֨ה מַעֲמִ֧יד בַּמֶּרְכָּבָ֛ה נֹ֥כַח אֲרָ֖ם עַד־הָעָ֑רֶב וַיָּ֕מָת לְעֵ֖ת בּ֥וֹא הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up the battle on that day, and [the] king of Israel was holding [himself] upright in the chariot opposite Aram until the evening; and he died at [the] time of [the] going of the sun.

en.L: And the battle went up on that day, and the king of Israel was holding [himself] upright in the chariot facing Aram until the evening; and he died at the time of the going of the sun.
en.B: All that day the battle grew fiercer, and the king of Israel kept himself upright in his chariot facing the Arameans until evening. At sunset he died.
en.R: The battle grew worse all that day. The king of Israel stayed propped up in his chariot, facing the Arameans, until evening. As the sun went down, he died.

es.L: Y arreció la batalla aquel día, y el rey de Israel se mantuvo de pie en el carro frente a Aram hasta la tarde; y murió a la hora de la puesta del sol.
es.B: Durante todo aquel día la batalla se hizo más intensa, y el rey de Israel se mantuvo de pie en su carro frente a los arameos hasta la tarde. Al ponerse el sol, murió.
es.R: La batalla empeoró durante todo aquel día. El rey de Israel se mantuvo sostenido en su carro, frente a los arameos, hasta la tarde. Cuando se puso el sol, murió.

fr.L: Et la bataille monta ce jour-là, et le roi d’Israël se tint debout dans le char face à Aram jusqu’au soir ; et il mourut au moment du coucher du soleil.
fr.B: La bataille devint de plus en plus violente ce jour-là, et le roi d’Israël se tint debout dans son char face aux Araméens jusqu’au soir. Au coucher du soleil, il mourut.
fr.R: La bataille est devenue de plus en plus terrible pendant toute la journée. Le roi d’Israël est resté debout dans son char, soutenu face aux Araméens, jusqu’au soir. Quand le soleil s’est couché, il est mort.

sw.L: Vita vikapanda siku ile, naye mfalme wa Israeli alikuwa akijitegemeza garini akiwaelekea Aramu mpaka jioni; akafa wakati wa kuzama kwa jua.
sw.B: Siku ile yote vita vikazidi kuwa vikali, naye mfalme wa Israeli akajishikilia wima garini akiwaelekea Waaramu mpaka jioni. Jua lilipozama, akafa.
sw.R: Vita vikazidi kuwa vibaya siku ile yote. Mfalme wa Israeli akabaki ameegemezwa garini mwake, akiwaelekea Waaramu, mpaka jioni. Jua lilipokuwa likizama, akafa.

vi.L: Ngày hôm ấy trận chiến dâng cao, và vua Y-sơ-ra-ên tự giữ mình đứng thẳng trong xe đối diện quân A-ram cho đến chiều; và vua chết lúc mặt trời lặn.
vi.B: Suốt ngày hôm ấy trận chiến càng thêm ác liệt, và vua Y-sơ-ra-ên gượng đứng trong xe, mặt hướng về quân A-ram cho đến chiều. Lúc mặt trời lặn thì vua chết.
vi.R: Suốt ngày hôm ấy trận chiến càng lúc càng dữ dội. Vua Y-sơ-ra-ên vẫn gượng đứng trong xe, mặt hướng về quân A-ram, cho đến chiều. Khi mặt trời lặn thì vua chết.

ko.L: 그리고 그날 싸움이 거세어졌고, 이스라엘 왕은 저녁까지 아람을 마주하여 병거 안에 버티고 서 있었다. 그리고 그가 해가 질 무렵에 죽었다.
ko.B: 그날 싸움은 종일 치열해졌고, 이스라엘 왕은 저녁까지 아람 군대를 마주한 채 병거 안에 버티고 서 있었다. 그는 해가 질 무렵에 죽었다.
ko.R: 그날 하루 종일 싸움은 점점 더 심해졌다. 이스라엘 왕은 저녁까지 아람 군대를 바라보며 병거 안에 기대어 서 있었다. 그리고 해가 질 때 죽었다.

pt.L: E a batalha subiu naquele dia, e o rei de Israel se manteve de pé no carro diante de Arã até a tarde; e morreu na hora do pôr do sol.
pt.B: A batalha foi ficando mais violenta durante todo aquele dia, e o rei de Israel se manteve de pé no seu carro, de frente para os arameus, até a tarde. Ao pôr do sol, ele morreu.
pt.R: A batalha foi piorando durante todo aquele dia. O rei de Israel ficou apoiado de pé no seu carro, de frente para os arameus, até a tarde. Quando o sol se pôs, ele morreu.

decisions.choice: Ahab's death told more briefly than in 1 Kings 22:35-38
decisions.reason: Kings says the king was propped up in the chariot and died in the evening, and that the blood of his wound ran into the chariot; it goes on to the army sent home, his burial in Samaria, and the dogs licking his blood as Yahweh had said (1 Kings 22:36-38). Chronicles ends with his death at sunset and does not name him again. Its story stays with Jehoshaphat, who returns safely to Jerusalem (19:1).

decisions.choice: was holding himself upright: an active form where Kings has "was propped up"
decisions.reason: Kings uses a passive form ("was made to stand"); Chronicles uses an active one ("was making stand"). It may mean that the king held himself up, or, with no object stated, that someone kept him upright. Either way he stayed upright in the chariot until he died.

decisions.choice: the battle went up: the battle rose, grew fierce
decisions.reason: The fighting increased in intensity through the day.

decisions.choice: upright in the chariot facing Aram: so the troops would not lose heart
decisions.reason: Instead of leaving the field as he had ordered (verse 33), the king stayed upright in his chariot, facing the enemy, perhaps so that his army would not see that he was wounded. He bled to death through the day.

decisions.choice: he died: Micaiah's word fulfilled
decisions.reason: The king does not "return in peace" (verses 26-27). As Micaiah had said, he died at Ramoth-gilead, and the flock was left without its shepherd (verse 16).

decisions.choice: grew fierce / grew worse
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "went up" means here (m3).

decisions.choice: At sunset / As the sun went down
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the time of the going of the sun" in ordinary words.

decisions.choice: "se mantuvo de pie"
decisions.reason: Chronicles uses an active form where 1 Kings 22:35 has "was propped up" (meaning decision); Spanish follows with the reflexive "se mantuvo".

decisions.choice: "tự giữ mình đứng thẳng" (L); "gượng đứng" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Chronicles has an active form where 1 Kings 22:35 has "was propped up" (m2): the king held himself up.

decisions.choice: "해가 질 무렵에" (L, B), "해가 질 때" (R)
decisions.reason: Chronicles ends with the king's death at sunset and leaves out the blood in the chariot; Korean follows its Hebrew.

decisions.choice: se manteve de pé (L, B), ficou apoiado de pé (R); até a tarde; ao pôr do sol
decisions.reason: The first words keep the Portuguese of 1 Kings 22:35 ("a batalha subiu", "foi ficando mais violenta", "foi piorando"); where Kings has the passive "was propped up", Chronicles has an active form (m2), so Literal and Balanced say "se manteve de pé", and Readable keeps Kings' "ficou apoiado de pé", as the English Readable keeps "propped up". Chronicles ends with the sunset and leaves out the blood (m1).
